office_does: The three county commissioners are the county's legislative body: they adopt the budget and county taxes, plan for growth, and build and run roads, the jail and other county facilities.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Janet St. Clair (D) is retiring, and the result decides the board's party majority. Republican Matthew Van Pelt led the district primary with 44.7%, and Democrat Grant Shaw edged a second Democrat for the other general-election spot; the general is county-wide.

candidates.summary: Camano Island resident of 30 years with a retail budget-management background and nonprofit and water-association leadership, making his first run for office; endorsed by Commissioner St. Clair and the Island County Democrats.
highlights: Supports a new jail with space for treatment, behavioral health and rehabilitation programs, funded partly through grants [S9]
Wants ADUs, smaller homes and workforce housing where infrastructure allows, with predictable permitting [S4]
Backs Growth Management planning that protects water, septic capacity, farmland and rural character [S4][S5]
Would review county operations for efficiency without cutting service levels [S9]
Says the ICOM 911 system needs an overhaul [S5]

spending.basis: Backs a new jail with program space, up-front technology investment and planning for future infrastructure, with no proposed cuts; also pledges to watch taxpayer dollars.

housing.basis: Mixed: more housing types and predictable permitting, limited by infrastructure and rural-character protection, with no public-housing or tenant proposals.

safety.basis: Frames a new jail around treatment, behavioral health and rehabilitation to reduce recidivism, while also pledging support for first responders.

experience.basis: First run for public office; brings retail budget and community-board leadership rather than a government record.

candidates.summary: North Whidbey resident, 23-year Navy veteran and owner of three local businesses, including a construction company, with no elected record; endorsed by the Island County Republican Party.
highlights: Says 'tax increases should be the last thing we look at' [S8]
Questions county-funded services he says draw newcomers to the island: 'We need to take care of who's already here' [S8]
Would look at remodeling the jail before building a new one [S8]
Would trim 'non-essential' building codes and cut permitting delays to lower construction costs [S4]
Wants funding to fill what he calls the state's lowest deputy staffing per resident [S4]

taxes.basis: Puts tax increases last and argues business growth and tourism would reduce pressure for further tax increases.

spending.basis: Focuses on cutting county costs, including county-funded social services, and prefers remodeling the jail, with volunteers rather than paid experts reviewing any new plans.

housing.basis: Would cut 'non-essential' building codes and permitting delays and opposes the state requirement to plan for population growth.

safety.basis: Repeatedly calls for more sheriff's deputies and law-enforcement presence and doubts in-jail treatment programs, while speaking of 'compassionate solutions' for strained services.

experience.basis: No elected record; runs on Navy and small-business experience for an open seat.
